title: Integer identity
prompt: `Integer a = 1000; Integer b = 1000;` — what is `a == b`?
options: `false` (usually) — == compares references, and 1000 is outside the -128..127 cache
explanation: Autoboxing caches -128..127, so with `Integer a = 100, b = 100;` the check `a == b` happens to be true — and then it breaks at 1000. Never `==` boxed types; use `.equals` or unbox to `int`.

title: Predict: the cache boundary
explanation: 127 is the top of the Integer cache, so `a` and `b` are the same object. 128 is boxed into two separate objects, so `==` (reference comparison) is false while `.equals` (value comparison) is true.

title: Predict: arrays in a HashSet
explanation: Arrays use identity `equals`/`hashCode`, so a new `int[]{0, 0}` is never found. The String key `"0,0"` compares by content. Other value-based keys: `r * cols + c`, `List.of(r, c)`, or a record.

title: Silent overflow
options: A negative number — int overflow wraps around silently
explanation: 4×10⁹ exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (~2.1×10⁹), wrapping to -294967296. Java throws NOTHING for int overflow. When sums can exceed 2.1 billion, compute in long: `(long) x + x`.

title: Predict: past MAX_VALUE
explanation: `max + 1` is int arithmetic and wraps around to `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, -2147483648. Casting `max` to `long` first makes the addition happen in `long`, giving the true 2147483648.

title: Predict: where the cast goes
prompt: `a` is 65536 (2¹⁶), so `a * a` is 2³² — too big for an `int`. Predict what each line prints.
explanation: In `(long) (a * a)` the multiplication runs in `int` first: 2³² wraps to exactly 0, and only then is 0 widened to `long`. In `(long) a * a` the cast binds to the first `a`, so the multiplication is done in `long` → 4294967296. Cast an operand, not the result.

title: The midpoint bug
prompt: In binary search, why write `int mid = l + (r - l) / 2;` instead of `(l + r) / 2`?
options: `l + r` can overflow int when both are large; `l + (r - l) / 2` cannot
explanation: With l and r both near 2 billion, l + r wraps negative and mid becomes garbage. This bug lived in the JDK's own binarySearch for nine years.

title: Predict: Math.abs edge case
explanation: The int range is -2147483648..2147483647, so +2147483648 doesn't exist. Negating `Integer.MIN_VALUE` overflows right back to itself, and `Math.abs` returns a negative number. If inputs can hit MIN_VALUE, work in `long`: `Math.abs((long) x)`.

title: Negative modulo
options: `-1` — the result takes the sign of the dividend
explanation: Java's % is a remainder, not a mathematical modulo. For a guaranteed non-negative result (circular indexing!): `((a % b) + b) % b`.

title: Predict: remainder vs floorMod
explanation: `%` keeps the sign of the left operand: -7 = 3 × (-2) + (-1). `Math.floorMod` always returns a result with the sign of the divisor, so 2. Adding `b` and taking `% b` again is the hand-rolled version of the same fix.

title: Predict: >> vs >>>
prompt: `-16` in binary is `1111...11110000` (32 bits). Predict what each line prints.
explanation: `>>` is an arithmetic shift: it copies the sign bit into the top, so a negative stays negative and `-16 >> 2` is -16 / 4 = -4. `>>>` is a logical shift: it fills with zeros, so the 28 bits shifted out leave only the top four 1-bits, `1111` = 15. Bit problems that treat an int as unsigned (Number of 1 Bits, Reverse Bits) need `>>>`.

title: The length gauntlet
prompt: Fill in the correct size access for each type — parentheses matter.
explanation: Array: field `.length`. String: method `.length()`. Collection: method `.size()`. Three APIs, three spellings — thanks, Java.

title: Predict: char arithmetic
explanation: `char + int` promotes to `int`: 'a' is 97, so 98. Cast back with `(char)` to get 'b'. Starting with a String makes `+` concatenate left to right: "a" then "a1". `'c' - 'a'` is 2 — the index trick behind every `int[26]` count array.

title: Concatenation cost
prompt: `String r = ""; for (...n times...) r += ch;` — total time?
options: O(n²) — each += copies the whole string so far; use StringBuilder for O(n)
explanation: 1 + 2 + ... + n copies ≈ n²/2. On a 10⁵-char build, that's the difference between instant and TLE.

title: Mutating while iterating
prompt: `for (Integer x : list) { if (x < 0) list.remove(x); }` — what happens?
options: ConcurrentModificationException (typically) — you can't structurally modify a list inside its own for-each
explanation: The for-each's hidden iterator notices the list changed under it. Use `list.removeIf(x -> x < 0)`, an explicit `Iterator` with `it.remove()`, or iterate by index backwards.

title: Predict: fixed-size lists
prompt: What does each marked line do? Write the value printed, or the exception's simple class name if it throws.
explanation: `Arrays.asList` returns a fixed-size view backed by an array: `set` works, but `add` and `remove` throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. (`List.of` is stricter still: even `set` throws.) Wrap it in `new ArrayList<>(...)` to get a normal, growable list.

title: Predict: null in an ArrayDeque
prompt: A tree BFS enqueues children without checking them. `root.left` is `null`. What happens on the marked line? Write the exception's simple class name.
explanation: `ArrayDeque` rejects `null` elements, because `poll`/`peek` use `null` to mean "empty". Guard each child: `if (node.left != null) queue.offer(node.left);`. (`LinkedList` allows nulls, which only hides the bug until you dereference one.)

title: Array default values
prompt: `new int[3]`, `new boolean[3]`, and `new Integer[3]` start filled with…
options: 0, false, and null respectively — and reading a null Integer into an int throws NPE
explanation: Primitives get zero-values; object arrays get null. `int x = integerArr[0];` on a fresh Integer[] is a NullPointerException at the unbox.
